rationales: Metallic bonds form among metal atoms, not between two non-metals.
Ionic bonds typically form by electron transfer between a metal and a non-metal.
Two non-metals commonly share electrons to form a covalent bond.
A coordinate covalent bond is a special shared-electron bond, not the expected general bond between two non-metals.
Benzene is non-polar and does not dissolve appreciably in water.
Sodium chloride is soluble in water.
Potassium bromide is soluble in water.
Magnesium chloride is soluble in water.
The long-form periodic table does not have 32 horizontal periods.
Eighteen is the number of vertical groups, not horizontal periods.
The long-form periodic table has seven horizontal periods.
Eight is not the number of horizontal periods in the long-form table.
Fluorine is the most electronegative halogen, not the least.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the least electronegativity among these halogens.
Cathode rays led to the discovery of the electron, not the proton.
Canal rays provided evidence for positively charged particles and led to the discovery of the proton.
X-rays are electromagnetic radiation and did not lead to the discovery of the proton.
Alpha rays are emitted by radioactive substances and are not credited with the discovery of the proton.
Mist consists of tiny liquid droplets dispersed in a gas, so it is liquid in gas.
Gas in liquid describes gas bubbles dispersed in a liquid, not mist.
Solid in gas describes smoke or dust in air, not mist.
Gas in solid is not the composition of mist.
Iodine has the least electronegativity among the listed halogens.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Fluorine is the most electronegative halogen.
Sugar solution does not produce ions in water and is a non-electrolyte.
Sodium chloride solution conducts electricity because it contains ions.
Sodium hydroxide solution conducts electricity because it contains ions.
Sulfuric acid solution conducts electricity because it ionizes in water.
Sulphur is generally dull rather than lustrous.
Phosphorus is not the lustrous non-metal in this list.
Iodine has a shiny, lustrous appearance.
Carbon is not generally considered lustrous in its common forms.
Soil is heterogeneous because its components are not uniformly distributed.
Rock is generally heterogeneous because it contains distinguishable mineral components.
Wood is heterogeneous in its structure and composition.
Ice cream is a colloid and is not a homogeneous mixture at the particle level.
Light water is ordinary water containing mostly protium, not deuterium.
Deuterium is used to make heavy water, D₂O.
Soft water is defined by low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions, not by deuterium.
Hard water contains dissolved mineral ions and is not made by using deuterium.
Group 15 contains the pnictogens, not the noble gases.
Group 16 contains the chalcogens, not the noble gases.
Group 17 contains the halogens, not the noble gases.
Group 18 is the noble-gas group.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
N₂ has a triple bond and each nitrogen has a complete octet.
O₂ has a double bond and each oxygen has a complete octet.
N₂ contains a triple covalent bond between its two nitrogen atoms.
O₂ contains a double covalent bond, not a triple bond.
H₂ contains a single covalent bond.
Cl₂ contains a single covalent bond.
HCl consists of two atoms per molecule, so it is diatomic.
H₂O has three atoms per molecule, so it is triatomic.
NO₂ has three atoms per molecule, so it is triatomic.
CO₂ has three atoms per molecule, so it is triatomic.
